rationale: A is better structured, more comprehensive, and more actionable across model design, training, validation, deployment, and rollout. Its PACS workflow uses broadly correct standards and patterns, including DICOMweb retrieval, DICOM SR output, and HL7v2 ORU^R01/FHIR reporting. B adds useful details such as patient-level validation splits and push-based C-STORE ingestion, but its apparent specificity is undermined by major technical errors: ORU^OBS and ORU^RSL are not standard HL7v2 message types, OBX-11 is result status rather than a value qualifier, its proposed LOINC mapping is questionable, and its sub-two-second whole-CT target is generally unrealistic. A still overstates some architecture, throughput, regulatory, and de-identification claims, but its core design is more sound and usable.
